comment: Shared cases for the RSVP active-word anchor: `last_started_index` /
`lastStartedIndex` / `__capRsvp.lastStartedIndex` — the index of the LAST word
so the rule is stated once for the three implementations.
This rule is deliberately NOT the `start <= t < end` test the decoration modes
use, and `activeInWindow` records what that test would answer — the FIRST index
whose window contains t, or -1 when no word's does — so every case says whether
the two rules agree. The cases where they
disagree are the whole point — an implementation that used the window test
would place the line, and colour the glyph, on a word that is not on the pivot
column. `reordered` and `overlapping` mirror the DISAGREEMENT_CASES in
backend/tests/test_rsvp_render.py, i.e. groups the renderer actually hits.
`count` is the optional upper bound on how many words to consider (null =
"all of them", which is Python `None` and `undefined` in both JS copies).
`t` is a number, or the string "NaN" — JSON has no NaN literal, so the

cases.name: before the first word
cases.why: nothing has started, so the anchor is word 0 rather than -1

cases.name: exactly at the first word's start
cases.why: the bound is inclusive: start <= t, not start < t

cases.name: exactly at a later word's start
cases.why: word 1 becomes the anchor on its own start frame, not one frame later

cases.name: inside a word
cases.why: the ordinary case, where both rules agree

cases.name: exactly at a word's end
cases.why: end is exclusive for the window test, so it already has no answer here; the anchor still holds word 1

cases.name: inside inter-word silence
cases.why: past word 1's end (1.0) and before word 2's start (1.2): the anchor HOLDS word 1 where the window test has no answer at all

cases.name: exactly at the last word's start
cases.why: the last word takes over on its start frame

cases.name: after the last word's end
cases.why: the group's tail hold: the last word stays the anchor, it does not reset to 0

cases.name: NaN t
cases.why: no comparison matches a NaN, so the loop never advances and the anchor is word 0

cases.name: single-word group, mid word
cases.why: one word is always the anchor

cases.name: single-word group, before it starts
cases.why: still 0 — the 'nothing started' fallback and the only word coincide

cases.name: empty word list
cases.why: defined as 0 rather than -1 or a throw, so callers need no empty branch

cases.name: reordered group, anchor is the displayed-second word
cases.why: manual word reorder: displayed order [bravo 1.50-2.00, alpha 1.00-1.50], so starts do not ascend. At t=1.20 only alpha has started

cases.name: reordered group, both started
cases.why: same reordered group at t=1.70 (test_rsvp_render's 'reordered' case): the window test answers bravo (0) but the line is parked on alpha (1), the LAST word to have started

cases.name: overlapping timings
cases.why: test_rsvp_render's 'overlapping' case: ascending starts, but alpha (1.00-1.60) is still inside its window when bravo (1.50-2.00) has begun, so the window test's FIRST answer is 0 while the anchor is 1

cases.name: count bounds the scan
cases.why: count 2 ignores word 2 entirely even though its start has long passed (line_offset_at passes count to skip words with no focus offset)

cases.name: count 1 pins the anchor to the first word
cases.why: a one-word window behaves exactly like a one-word group

cases.name: count 0 considers nothing
cases.why: an empty window is the empty-list answer, not a crash

cases.name: count past the end is clamped
cases.why: a ragged caller must not index off the end; min(count, len(words)) wins
